items.title: Valley Line West Final Traffic Configuration
items.source_date: Date not stated on retrieved page

citations.finding: The City says 102 Avenue between 107 Street and 102 Street was permanently reduced to one eastbound lane in connection with Valley Line West. This is a relevant alternative explanation for the commenter’s broader reference to 102 Avenue east of 109 Street; it does not establish that the lane was removed for a bike lane.
citations.establishes: A permanent traffic-lane reduction on a 102 Avenue segment attributed to LRT accommodation, rather than establishing a bike-lane conversion.

citations.finding: The City attributes 102 Avenue's permanent reduction between 107 and 102 Street to accommodation of Valley Line West LRT. Its summer 2026 update says that section was temporarily closed for LRT construction and its bike lanes had been temporarily relocated to 103 Avenue. Those records do not establish that bike lanes caused the claimed loss of through lanes east of 109 Street.
citations.establishes: A distinct LRT reason for a downtown 102 Avenue lane reduction. The construction update is at https://www.edmonton.ca/projects_plans/transit/valley-line-west.

items.title: 102 Avenue Bike Route (111–136 Street) Fact Sheet
items.source_date: 2017; exact publication date not stated in the retrieved document

citations.finding: The fact sheet says 102 Avenue from 121 Street to 111 Street was then a two-way roadway and would be converted to one-way eastbound, with parking remaining on the south side. The City’s November 2017 brochure confirms the one-way configuration and new bike routes. Together these records support a through-lane reallocation associated with a bike route on this segment; the exact lane-by-lane design should be checked against the project drawings.
citations.establishes: The segment’s prior two-way operation, planned one-way eastbound conversion, and parking remaining on the south side. It does not alone establish a citywide corridor count.
citations.quote: 102 Avenue from 121 Street to 111 Street is currently a two-way roadway.

citations.finding: The May 2017 fact sheet identifies 102 Avenue, 121–111 Street, as previously two-way and specifies removal of its westbound travel lane to fit the protected bike lane. The City's subsequent route guide describes the avenue as now one-way eastbound.
citations.establishes: Prior through-lane use, the lane selected for removal, the bike-lane design and its stated reason on this segment; the completion check is in the 2017 route guide.

items.title: On Hermitage Road, bike lanes, shared use paths, budget pressures, and WHY

citations.finding: The councillor's account of Hermitage Road (2024, Towards 40 program) describes narrowed lanes, buffered bike lanes, removal of slip lanes and closure of one of two left-turn lanes at 50 Street. It does not describe removal of a through lane.
citations.establishes: That a prominent northeast bike-lane project is not shown to be a through-lane conversion on the evidence found.

items.title: 102 Avenue protected bike lane from 99 St to 107 St

citations.finding: The 2015 102 Avenue downtown redesign combined a south-side two-way cycle track, north-side two-way Valley Line LRT and centre-running one-way vehicle travel.
citations.establishes: That any vehicle-lane loss on 102 Ave east of 109 St is shared with the LRT, so it cannot be attributed to the bike lane alone.

items.title: City to spend big bucks to remove bike lanes on 95th Avenue

citations.finding: The 2013 95 Avenue lanes were designed to keep the same number of driving lanes through most of the route by narrowing lanes and removing about 14 blocks of parking. Those lanes, and the 40 Ave and 106 St lanes, were removed after a July 2015 council vote.
citations.establishes: That some outer-area bike lanes took parking rather than through lanes, and that those lanes are no longer in the inventory.

items.title: Edmonton bike lane project met with provincial opposition

citations.finding: In a letter dated 2025-04-16, Alberta's transportation minister asked the City to cancel or postpone 132 Ave bike lanes between 66 and 97 Street over 'driving capacity', about 7,000 vehicles per day.
citations.establishes: That the province characterized the 132 Ave project as reducing road capacity. This corroborates the lane reduction but is not a City record.

items.title: Here's why Edmonton's 132nd Avenue renewal project is garnering attention (CBC); City 132 Avenue Renewal project page and Stage 5 FAQ as surfaced in search

citations.finding: City officials describe narrowing 132 Avenue from four lanes to two (in the sections that had two each way) as traffic calming, with the space reallocated to wider sidewalks, trees and a separated bike lane in each direction, between 127 Street and Fort Road. West section construction began May 2023; the full project is due fall 2027.
citations.establishes: That the City states it is reducing through lanes on 132 Ave and putting bike lanes in the freed space. City document text was seen only via search excerpts; direct fetch of edmonton.ca failed with HTTP 502.

citations.establishes: A completed 2025 conversion of the former southbound motor-vehicle through movement into space for an on-street protected bike lane.

citations.finding: The City's project table says the proposed 95 Avenue route, including removal of a vehicle travel lane in each direction from 149 to 156 Street, was postponed and remained at pre-construction; it cannot be counted as a built conversion by the as-of date.

items.title: 83 Avenue Pre-Construction Meeting, pp. 2, 8; Southside Pre-Construction Display, p. 8
items.source_date: April 6, 2017; no separate last-updated date stated; March 2018 construction-status document also consulted

citations.finding: The April 6, 2017 pre-construction display describes 83 Avenue, 99–106 Street, as a two-lane local roadway to become eastbound-only for cars, except 102–104 Street, with protected bike lanes. A March 2018 City display says the 95A–106 Street portion had been constructed in 2016 and 2017.
citations.establishes: Prior through-lane use and the specified conversion on the 83 Avenue project. Completion is corroborated by https://www.edmonton.ca/public-files/assets/document?path=RoadsTraffic%2FSouthsideDisplayBoards16-03-18.pdf.

items.title: 132 Avenue Renewal: Urban Design Analysis
items.source_date: 2022; exact publication date not stated in the retrieved document

citations.finding: The City’s 132 Avenue Urban Design Analysis says the roadway configuration varies; with parking, most sections generally operate with one lane in each direction, although some sections and service roads appear wider. This does not establish that through lanes were removed to make room for bike facilities, and cautions against treating every 132 Avenue bike facility as a qualifying lane conversion.
citations.establishes: The variable existing roadway configuration and the limitation of inferring prior through-lane use from the presence of a bike facility.
citations.quote: with parking it generally operates as one lane in each direction

items.title: 132 Avenue Renewal: Exploring Options and Tradeoffs, p. 13
items.source_date: 2020; no separate last-updated date stated; the 2022 What We Decided report and project page last updated September 1, 2026 were also consulted

citations.finding: For 132 Avenue, the City's 2020 options document lists particular sections where driving lanes would be reduced, while its 2022 final-decision report specifies one driving lane in each direction and raised bike paths. The project was a broader street renewal. The City's page records completion of the 101–107 Street section in 2023, but I could not verify whether its raised paths appear in the specified on-street inventory layer. I therefore do not add 132 Avenue to C or A.
citations.establishes: The named 132 Avenue example concerns specific prior driving-lane reductions, not every section of the avenue; final design and construction are documented at https://www.edmonton.ca/sites/default/files/public-files/132AveRenewal_WhatWeDecided.pdf and https://www.edmonton.ca/transportation/on_your_streets/132-avenue-renewal.

citations.finding: The City brochure states that 102 Avenue was one-way eastbound from 121 Street to 111 Street and identifies the new West Central Bike Routes. This corroborates the completed directional change and bike-route installation.

citations.quote: 102 Avenue is now one-way for vehicle traffic heading east from 121 Street to 111 Street.

items.title: City of Edmonton GIS, Bike Routes - On Street, statistics grouped by street and classification

citations.finding: Built protected-lane features (444 in total) are concentrated on central and north-side streets. Suburban painted lanes (e.g. Saddleback Rd, Wolf Willow Rd, 141 St SW, Leger Rd, 19/29/31 Ave, 40 St, 82 St, 69 Ave, 139 Ave) have null construction years, and I found no record that any of them replaced a through lane.
citations.establishes: Where bike facilities are, which bounds the possible spread of conversions. It does not establish prior lane use either way.

citations.finding: The inventory layer has 3,175 features, matching the brief's snapshot count. 132 AVENUE NW carries 72 protected-bike-lane features plus 1 EB and 1 WB, with construction_year 2023–2025. 102 AVENUE NW carries 27 protected features dated 2016–2022.
citations.establishes: That bike facilities exist on 132 Ave and 102 Ave in the City's inventory, and their recorded construction years. It does not establish prior lane use.

citations.finding: Near St. Cecilia Junior High and the O'Leary Leisure Centre, 132 Ave was 'effectively seven lanes of road plus service road' before renewal and became four car lanes plus boulevard, wider sidewalk and bike lanes.
citations.establishes: Advocate's description of the lane change on one 132 Ave section. Lead only.

items.title: Vehicles going wrong way on 102nd Avenue (Edmonton Journal, via PressReader; content seen through search, direct fetch returned 403)

citations.finding: When the permanent protected lane opened in Oliver on 2017-11-14, 102 Avenue went from two-way traffic to a single lane between 111 and 121 Street, and drivers were reported travelling the wrong way.
citations.establishes: Reported conversion from two-way to one-way on the named segment, consistent with the commenter's example. No City document was retrieved.
